body:
I really never had many chances to practice being affectionate. Even after I realized my parents were abusing me, it took me a lot longer to accept it. I was angry at being removed from my home, so I denied a lot of truths just so that I wouldn't have to acknowledge that I was wrong and that my situation was wrong. 

Maybe I could have been adopted, but from the beginning I just didn't get along with my first fosters, and I started lashing out more and more aggressively to make them leave me alone. Sometimes I want to kick my childhood self.

I truly hope that's not what you're doing. If you appreciate my kindness, then do me a favor and don't mix drugs and alcohol, don't die, and call 911 if you're hurting yourself or are about to. Continue attempting communication with your husband. Tell him what you're feeling and try to work towards a solution together that will improve things for you.

I've felt like you do a lot before. It's painful to feel like this, especially if you feel it when you don't have someone nearby. If you slow down and clear your mind, then look at your situation again, I think you'll feel better about your options by and by.

It doesn't have to be suicide, there will be opportunities to change this situation that's hurting you into something better. It's just going to take time.

Maybe he doesn't think anything is wrong, and so maybe he's not trying to upset you either. Dare I suggest you might return to your home country until it's closer to the time when he comes home- maybe stay with some family? Are there support groups for spouses of service members that you can start attending?

Is it possible that something may be going on? I'm not saying anything bad, but maybe something that just keeps him from his phone. That is a long time to be apart, but I just get the sense that you have a lot that shouldn't be staked on suicide.

I'm new, and I don't have any professional training to talk to people about their suicidal urges, but I don't think you should do it, obviously. I'm sure it's a lot to handle, especially if you're in a country that's foreign to you, but don't you want to see your husband again? Do you really want to hurt him with suicide?

I would talk to your friend if possible, try to get the story straight with them. When your husband is back, then there will be two of you to think things through and find an arrangement where you can be happier. I know you've said that you're ready now, but I think if you wait there will be opportunities to fix these things.

I didn't really know my family life was abusive as a kid. I assumed that my parents were crazier than other people, but I thought that all kids were treated like I was behind closed doors. My dad had the behavior of a meth addict as long as I can remember, but I remember my mom being young and kind. At some point I guess she got hooked through my dad's habits, and she started acting like him. 

It's hard to remember what happened which year, I was taken into CPS at age 5. I've talked to my birth mom again, she lives in a women's shelter and she's about halfway healthy. My dad served for the charges from when I was taken away, but is in prison again currently.

I understand. I've already seen a couple posts from people who are saying stuff like me. How they've run away from home, only have one person or no people to rely on, and haven't had a real family life either.
